_note: Invented precincts covering the playable area (E8). Real NYPD precinct numbers and houses are not used. 'corruptibility' is 0-5 (how cheaply reports go away). 'payoffs' ties the story's pad to the bribe system: flags move corruptibility. Gameplay owns the mechanics.

precincts.name: Midtown Central
precincts.covers: W 29th to W 43rd St, 6th Ave west to the edge (the Garment District, Penn Station, the Deuce, Eighth Ave)
precincts.why: Wurtz's plainclothes 'conditions' unit works out of here. Collections are routine, and reports are cheap to lose.

payoffs.effect: Teddy's own reports cost less to bury (he carries their envelopes)
corruptibility drops to 1 in the epilogue (unit suspended)
corruptibility drops to 2 (unit disbanded, the rest scared)
corruptibility 5, but only for Teddy: the new pad

honest: char.pat_kearney (won't take money; can be persuaded by relationship)

precincts.name: Madison Square
precincts.covers: W 22nd to W 29th St, the edge east to Madison (Flatiron, Madison Sq Park, the Flower and Fur Districts, Penn South)
precincts.why: An old-fashioned house: the florists and furriers pay small at Christmas, but nobody organises it. Since the Commission, nervous.
honest: char.sgt_bauman (takes a Christmas turkey, never cash)

precincts.name: Bryant Park
precincts.covers: W 29th to W 43rd St, 6th Ave east to the edge (Herald Square, Fifth Ave offices, the Library, Bryant Park)
precincts.why: Fifth Avenue money wants a clean precinct. Bribes are expensive and risky here. Greer files everything twice.

payoffs.effect: Nick's reports here are 'lost' (the Special Prosecutor's protection)

honest: char.det_fisk (Internal Affairs; hunts players who bribe too often citywide)

reports.note: Per the CORE_SYSTEMS design: witnesses run to red police call boxes; each precinct keeps reports with descriptions (lead, clothing colours, vehicle). Narrative supplies the text below.
reports.callBoxColour: red (period police call boxes on lampposts)
